paragraphs.text: Cornelia de Lange syndrome-4 (CDLS4) is a cohesinopathy. Affected individuals have growth retardation, minor skeletal anomalies, and facial features that overlap those of Cornelia de Lange syndrome (CdLS). Cognitive impairment is much milder than in classic CdLS caused by mutations in NIPBL, SMC1A, or SMC3 (Deardorff et al., 2012). Compared with CdLS caused by NIPBL or SMC1A variants, the phenotype is attenuated for facial morphology, limb anomalies, and especially cognition and behavior. Some patients have holoprosencephaly, with or without CdLS features. The disorder varies markedly between and within families (Krab et al., 2020).

paragraphs.text: Krab et al. (2020) studied 49 individuals from 33 families with RAD21 alterations, including 24 previously unpublished cases. Patients came from Australia, Belgium, Canada, Denmark, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Turkey, the United Kingdom, and the United States. Full clinical data were available for 29 individuals from 22 families (cohort A), whose ages ranged from 0 to 61 years (median 9 years). All patients in cohort A had CdLS scores of at least 5. CdLS had been suspected before testing in about 60% of index cases. Compared with NIPBL and SMC1A cohorts, Krab et al. (2020) found that CdLS features in cohort A were less prevalent and typically less severe. Frequent features were: - long and/or smooth philtrum (90%) - short nose (88%) - concave nasal ridge (83%) - thick eyebrows (83%) - short fifth finger (82%) - long eyelashes (81%) - thin upper lip vermilion (79%) - upturned nasal tip (70%) - synophrys (68%) - arched eyebrows (67%) - low anterior/posterior hairline (61%) - postnatal head circumference less than -2 SD (57%) - clinodactyly of the fifth finger (54%) - low-set and/or malformed ears (54%) - gastroesophageal reflux (52%) - dislocated elbow or abnormal elbow extension (46%) - abnormal palmar crease (43%) - ptosis (42%) - heart anomalies (39%) - hirsutism (38%) - postnatal height less than -2 SD (37%) - micrognathia (35%) - hearing loss (33%) - cleft palate or submucous cleft palate (24%) No patient had a major limb malformation, and hands and feet were generally of normal size. Minor anomalies of the hands and feet were common, including fetal pads, abnormal flexion crease patterns, and camptodactyly. Growth at birth was generally less impaired than in the other cohorts, and short stature and microcephaly developed postnatally. Seizures occurred in 9%, and none of 24 patients had visual impairment. Krab et al. (2020) also noted some unusual anomalies: - vertebral anomalies (clefts and hemivertebrae) - malformations of structures derived from the embryonic foregut - occasional diaphragmatic hernia, anal atresia, or choanal atresia

paragraphs.text: In cohort A, cognition and behavior were also less affected than in the NIPBL and SMC1A groups (Krab et al., 2020). Sixteen of the 29 patients (55%) had normal or mildly impaired cognitive function. No patient had severe or profound disability. All patients aged 3 years and older used some words, and language problems were more prominent than motor problems. Fourteen of 25 patients (56%) had behavioral problems, mainly anxiety, ADHD, autism spectrum disorder, and obsessive-compulsive behavior. Aggression and self-injurious behavior were uncommon. Within families, variation in cognition and behavior could be considerable: some families included both patients with intellectual disability and patients with apparently normal cognition. Some carriers were diagnosed only after more severely affected offspring were recognized. Among the 20 individuals with limited clinical data (cohort B), additional phenotypes included Mungan syndrome (in patients with biallelic variants) and holoprosencephaly, with or without CdLS characteristics.

paragraphs.text: The heterozygous RAD21 mutations in CDLS4 occur de novo or are inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern. Minor et al. (2014) reported the first familial case, in which an in-frame deletion was inherited from a mother with a mild phenotype. Boyle et al. (2017) found a RAD21 variant in a mildly affected index patient, her mother, and 2 aunts, and suggested that RAD21 variants show incomplete penetrance. In the series of Krab et al. (2020), 9 of 21 index cases with known inheritance were familial. The authors noted marked intrafamilial and interfamilial variability.

paragraphs.text: Deardorff et al. (2012) found mutations in the cohesin structural gene RAD21 in children with a CdLS-like phenotype. The mutations acted at the interface between RAD21 and the other cohesin proteins STAG2 and SMC1A. They impaired the cellular DNA damage response and disrupted transcription in a zebrafish model. paragraphs.text: In a patient (IV.16) with mild CdLS (CDLS4), Boyle et al. (2017) identified a heterozygous 1-bp deletion in the RAD21 gene (c.704delG), predicted to cause a frameshift and premature stop codon (Ser235IlefsTer19). The deletion was also found in the patient's mother and 2 aunts, who did not fulfill the diagnostic criteria for CdLS. Krab et al. (2020) placed the deletion in exon 7. They reported an additional affected family member carrying it and gave the family members CdLS scores of 9 to 12.

paragraphs.text: In a 15-month-old boy with CDLS4, Gudmundsson et al. (2019) used exome sequencing to identify a de novo heterozygous 3-bp deletion in the RAD21 gene (c.1774_1776del), resulting in deletion of gln592 (Gln592del). The boy had developmental delay, CdLS-like facial features, reflux, testis retention, prominent digit pads, and diaphragmatic hernia. In silico structural modeling predicted disturbance of the RAD21-SMC1A interface. Molecular dynamics modeling by Krab et al. (2020) predicted that the deletion moves lys605 away from ATPase site 1 of the SMC1A/SMC3 heads.
